# Buddhist Creator Connector

Find, read, cite and compare Buddhist texts from the WeBuddhist Library: Tibetan canon, translations, commentaries, chants and recordings.

## How the library is organised

WeBuddhist Library: Buddhist texts (Tibetan canon and more), their editions, translations, commentaries, segments, alignments, people and recordings.
Id kinds: a *text* is a work; an *edition* is a readable version of a text (read_edition, list_segments need an edition id); a *segment* is a paragraph/verse of an edition.
Typical flow: search_texts or search_content -> get_text (to see editions) -> read_edition (window) or get_full_content (whole text) or list_segments -> get_aligned_segments to compare with a translation.
Content positions are Unicode code points, end-exclusive. Lists have no totals; follow next_offset while has_more.

Load the matching skill before answering; each one names the exact tool sequence to use.

| `build-reading-list` | Build a curated, cited reading list from the WeBuddhist Library for a topic, category, tag, author or language (for example "Prajnaparamita texts with English translations" or "chants by Nagarjuna"). Use when the user asks what to read, for recommendations, a syllabus, a study plan, a bibliography, or an overview of which texts exist on a subject. | `browse_categories`, `list_tags`, `list_languages`, `search_texts`, `get_text`, `search_persons`, `get_person` |
| `cite-buddhist-text` | Quote a passage from a Buddhist text verbatim with an exact library citation (text, edition, segment reference, span). Use when the user asks to quote, cite, source, verify, locate or check the wording of a line, verse, mantra or passage from a sutra, tantra, commentary, prayer or chant, in Tibetan, English or another language, or asks "where does it say" / "what is the exact wording". | `search_texts`, `search_content`, `get_text`, `get_segment`, `read_edition`, `get_full_content` |
| `compare-translations` | Show a Buddhist text and its translation side by side, segment by segment, using the library's alignments (for example Tibetan original beside the English translation). Use when the user asks to compare translations, see the original next to a translation, check how a line was translated, or find the Tibetan for an English passage (or vice versa). | `search_texts`, `search_content`, `get_text`, `get_aligned_segments`, `get_segment`, `list_segments` |

## Tools (MCP server `webuddhist-library`)

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `search_texts` | Find texts (works) in the library by title and/or filters. |
| `get_text` | Full record for one text: all titles, language, category, contributors (authors, translators), its editions (pass an edition id to read_edition / list_segments), and the titles of its translations and commentaries. |
| `read_edition` | Read the text of an edition as plain text, a window at a time. |
| `get_full_content` | Fetch the complete text of an edition in one call. |
| `search_content` | Full-text search inside the content of editions (not titles; use search_texts for titles). |
| `get_segment` | One segment (a paragraph/verse/line unit of an edition) with its text and position. |
| `list_segments` | Page through the segments (paragraphs/verses) of an edition in reading order, with their text. |
| `get_aligned_segments` | Segment-by-segment alignment between two editions, e.g. |
| `get_edition` | Metadata for one edition (a concrete readable version of a text) plus which other editions it is aligned with and its audio recordings. |
| `search_persons` | Find people (authors, translators, teachers) by name or BDRC/Wikidata id. |
| `get_person` | One person's record (all name forms, BDRC/Wikidata ids) and the first page of texts they contributed to.. |
| `browse_categories` | Navigate the category tree used to classify texts. |
| `list_tags` | All tags that can be applied to texts (e.g. |
| `list_languages` | Language codes used by the library (for search_texts.language, get_segment.related_language).. |
| `get_recording` | Metadata for an audio recording of an edition (reciter, format, duration) and a temporary playable URL. |
